method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the sentences the article relies on were located in the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source.

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Liquidity Sweep
what_it_says: A run through a level where resting orders cluster that then fails to hold beyond it; the classic form is a wick through a prior swing high or low.
States that definitions are contested at the edges: some traders require the close back inside on the sweeping candle, others accept any tag-and-reject that resolves within a few bars.
Treats grab, purge, raid, stop run and stop hunt as names for the same footprint.
FAQ: 'stop hunt' implies an intent that a chart cannot prove; 'liquidity sweep' is the neutral term.
not_specified: how many bars define the swing
how far price must go through the level
how many bars it has to come back

definition_sources.name: TMGM academy: Liquidity Sweep
what_it_says: Price moves beyond an established level and fails to maintain acceptance beyond it; needs a pre-existing level, a breach and a rejection or reclaim.
FAQ: a wick alone is not enough.
Lists 'penetration threshold' and 'reclaim window' as detector settings without giving values.
Some traders use sweep and grab as synonyms; others use grab for a faster single-candle event and sweep for a broader move.

definition_sources.name: LiteFinance blog: Liquidity Sweep
definition_sources.page_date: datePublished 2026-08-17, dateModified 2026-08-31 (schema.org metadata in the page)
what_it_says: Price briefly crosses a level where stop-loss orders are concentrated; the move typically leaves a long wick.
Calls a sweep a form of market manipulation by larger participants.
Says a liquidity grab is the broader concept (absorption of any pending orders), which is the reverse of the TMGM and FXOpen usage.

definition_sources.name: FXOpen blog: Liquidity Sweep in Trading
definition_sources.page_date: Published 29 Dec 2025 (article:modified_time 2026-01-23 in the page's metadata)
what_it_says: Describes large institutional participants intentionally driving price towards liquidity zones.
A grab may move slightly beyond a peak or low before reversing; a sweep can see a sustained movement beyond it before reversing.
Says sweeps often resemble false breakouts, without separating the two.

related_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: False Breakout
what_it_says: A close back inside the level is the common trigger that reclassifies a break as false; it often happens within a few bars.
Presents a liquidity sweep as the Smart Money Concepts description of similar price action; a false breakout can apply to any level and may stay beyond it for several bars.

related_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Turtle Soup
what_it_says: Credits the setup to Laurence Connors and Linda Raschke, Street Smarts (1995).

Original buy rule as the page states it: a new 20-day low while the previous 20-day low is at least four sessions old; entry on a buy stop back above the prior low; initial stop below the new extreme.
related_sources.caveat: We have not read the book. The attribution and the rules are as this page gives them.
